01Why now

Why this course, and why now

Agents read untrusted text and then act: they send, spend, change records and run code. That makes the model the wrong place to rely on for safety. This course is built on one rule: the model may propose an action, but independently enforced policy decides whether that action is allowed to affect the world.

02Outcomes

What you will be able to do

Threat-model an agent

Map what an agent can read, remember, call and change, and where each attack can enter.

Enforce policy outside the model

Design identity, tool access, sandboxing and approvals so a manipulated model still cannot do harm.

Plan attack tests

Design authorised red-team and adaptive evaluations for an agent (lessons 16 and 21), write the test plan for an MCP server (lesson 26), and judge results fairly. You run the example attacks in the local reference kit; running tests on live systems is your own authorised work.

Detect, respond and govern

Monitor agents, contain an incident, recover, and keep the evidence an auditor or insurer will ask for.

04The lab

Write the assurance pack for one agent system

Across the course you write one assurance pack for an agent system you know: one lab section per lesson, 28 in all. The labs are design and planning work, with a model solution and a rubric for each. You do not attack your own systems in the course; practice tools and a local reference kit let you run example controls and attacks on synthetic data. One pack, built in steps after each lesson. Each step has instructions, a model solution and a rubric to mark your own work, and saves on your device. The health check confirms the pack is complete and free of placeholders and secrets. It does not judge whether your security design is right; that needs a human reviewer.

The steps

  1. Lesson 1: Draw the system boundary and assign security ownership
  2. Lesson 2: Build a component, identity and data-flow map
  3. Lesson 3: Produce an agentic threat model and risk register
  4. Lesson 4: Map attack patterns to controls and test cases
  5. Lesson 5: Run a safe prompt-injection defense tabletop
  6. Lesson 6: Review an MCP server's trust and authorization posture
  7. Lesson 7: Design delegated identity and least-privilege grants
  8. Lesson 8: Design a secure RAG and memory lifecycle
  9. Lesson 9: Specify secure inter-agent contracts and delegation
  10. Lesson 10: Write a sandbox security profile and test plan
  11. Lesson 11: Create an AI supply-chain inventory and release gate
  12. Lesson 12: Design cloud guardrails for an agent runtime
  13. Lesson 13: Create a secure reference architecture and ADR
  14. Lesson 14: Specify and test a runtime authorization policy
  15. Lesson 15: Build an agentic audit event and detection plan
  16. Lesson 16: Design a reproducible agent security evaluation
  17. Lesson 17: Run an agentic incident-response tabletop
  18. Lesson 18: Build an agent governance and assurance pack
  19. Lesson 19: Create sector assurance profiles
  20. Lesson 20: Capstone: design, test and defend a secure agentic enterprise
  21. Lesson 21: Write an adaptive evaluation plan for one control
  22. Lesson 22: Map sources to sinks and write sink policies
  23. Lesson 23: Write a containment spec and run a drill
  24. Lesson 24: Plan an exposure measurement and write-path controls
  25. Lesson 25: Write three runtime rules and a fair detection test
  26. Lesson 26: Write the authorization test plan for an MCP server
  27. Lesson 27: Build a skill and tool register with review rules
  28. Lesson 28: Design agent identity, delegation and revocation

What the health check looks for

  • All 28 section headings are present
  • Every section has been started
  • Every task in a started section has a real answer (12 words or more)
  • No placeholder text is left in started sections
  • Nothing in the pack looks confidential

06Certificate

A certificate you can verify and share

When you meet the criteria you can claim a certificate with its own credential ID and a public page anyone can open to verify it. Add it to LinkedIn in one click, share it, or save it as a PDF.

To earn it

  1. Finish every lesson
  2. Complete every lab step and pass its health checks
  3. Answer at least 70% of the check questions correctly, on the first try or in review

What you get

  • A credential ID and a public page that confirms it
  • Add to LinkedIn in one click
  • Share on LinkedIn, X or Facebook, or copy the link
  • Save as a PDF

Intellica certificates show that you finished this course, as reported by your own browser and checked against the course's completion rules. The record is self-reported: it is not proctored, and your lab work is not marked by Intellica. They are not accredited qualifications and do not lead to any outside certification.
